full_judgment:
2. Short facts necessary for disposal of this petition for leave to appeal are that on 04.07.1980, the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 259 of 1980 in the Court of Munsif, Sirajganj impleading the respondents as defendants for declaration of title in respect of 1.83 acres of land out of 9.80 acres described in the schedule- 'Ka and 'Kha' to the plaint on the averments inter-alia, that during the C.S. operation 9.80 acres of land appertaining to C.S. plot No. 8415 were recorded in abstract Khatian as 1 Chemair river in the name of Dinesh Chandra Chowdhury and Motwalli Md. Aktar Ali Talukder of Amiruddin Wakf Estate. After the said land became cultivable the plaintiff got 'Ka' schedule land measuring an area of 1.28 acres from three sons of Dinesh Chaddra Roy Chowdhury, namely, Bupesh Chandra Roy, Bhupati Chandra Roy and Bhupendra Chandra Roy by way of pattan on 15th Ashwin, 1348 B.S. The plaintiff also got 0.55 acre of land as described in schedule-'Kha' to the plaint from Aktar Ali Talukder by way of pattan on 15th Ashar, 1350 B.S. The plaintiff I executed a kabuliat in favour of Zamindar for the 'Ka' schedule land on 1st Kartik, 1348 B.S. and since then he has been possessing the same in exercise of his right and title. During S.A. operation the Land was recorded in abstract Khatian of the Government for which the title of the plaintiff was clouded; hence the suit. 

 5. The case of defendant No. 2 was that the suit land measuring an area of 9.80 acres originally belonged to Zamindar Amiruddin Talukder and Dinesh Chandra Roy Chowdhury. On the basis of amicable settlement Amiruddin Talukder got the entire land who died leaving behind one son Akbar Ali Talukder as his heir. He got 2.00 acres of land including the suit land claimed by the plaintiff by way of pattan in 1350 B.S. and during S.A. operation the land was duly recorded in his name in S.A. Khatian No. 985. During liberation war all his documents were lost. The plaintiff has been claiming the suit land by creating some fictitious documents. The plaintiff had no right, title and possession in the suit land, therefore, the suit was liable to he dismissed.
